newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Synthetic Rubber to raise prices.
newsitem.headline: Japan Synthetic Rubber to raise prices.

text.p: Japan Synthetic Rubber Co Ltd said on Thursday it will raise its benchmark synthetic rubber price by 10 percent from the current 140 yen per kg, effective from January.
The price hike for styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) will be the first since the end of 1994, a company spokesman said.
He said the move was in response to rising prices of raw materials such as ethylene, caused by higher naphtha prices.
"We are aiming to improve profitability, as raw material prices are climbing due to higher naphtha prices," the spokesman said.
Nearby naphtha cargo prices were quoted at $244.0 per tonne on a cost and freight basis as of December 11, sharply up from around $170.0 one year ago.
Other leading synthetic rubber makers such as Nippon Zeon Co Ltd are likely to follow suit, industry sources said.

Synthetic rubber is used mainly to make tyres. Of Japan's total rubber consumption of 1.77 million tonnes in 1995, synthetic rubber accounted for 61.1 percent, according to the Japan Rubber Manufacturers' Association.
